agenda: Threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: The United States’ objectives are to prevent an ISIL/Da’esh resurgence after the collapse of the Assad regime, reinforce sanctions and border/financing cooperation, and keep humanitarian access and accountability in the text while supporting the UN-led political process. The main difficulties will be Russian and Chinese sensitivity to accountability language, any implication of endorsing cross-border or coalition operations, and competing views on the balance between counter-terrorism measures and humanitarian carve-outs.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the draft’s focus on countering ISIL/Da’esh, upholding Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, and preserving humanitarian access. We request explicit reaffirmation that the 1267 listing and delisting processes remain Member State-driven and that the Monitoring Team’s work is not politicized, and that references to 'other terrorist groups' be tied to Security Council designations. We would also like the text to recall the principle of non-refoulement in the context of returns.
messages.China: China supports the Council's firm condemnation of terrorism in Syria and the emphasis on Syria's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We ask that the text explicitly name the East Turkestan Islamic Movement, strengthen Member States' responsibility for their foreign terrorist fighters, and address the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures on humanitarian access and counter-terrorism cooperation. With these adjustments, China can support the draft.
messages.Denmark: Denmark supports the draft’s strong condemnation of ISIL/Da’esh and its balanced focus on humanitarian access, accountability and sanctions implementation. We ask the penholder to strengthen explicit compliance with international human rights, refugee and humanitarian law in OP3, and to reinforce child-sensitive safeguards in OP5, including the best interests of the child and prevention of statelessness. We would also like a new operative paragraph on women’s full, equal and meaningful participation in counter-terrorism and reintegration efforts. Denmark can support the text with these adjustments.
messages.France: France supports the thrust of the US draft and its focus on ISIL/Da’esh, humanitarian access and accountability. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP4 on access across borders and conflict lines, OP5 on a child-rights-based approach to repatriation and reintegration, OP6 on cooperation with the IIIM and survivor-centred accountability, and OP11 on women’s full and equal participation. We also propose a new operative paragraph on a comprehensive strategy for the al-Hol and Roj camps.
messages.Greece: Greece supports the draft’s focus on ISIL/Da’esh, humanitarian access and accountability. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP5 and OP11 with explicit non-refoulement and best-interests-of-the-child safeguards, and to add protection of religious and ethnic minorities, including Christians, and humanitarian personnel in OP4. We also seek minor language in OP7 confirming that sanctions implementation is consistent with international law and humanitarian exemptions.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the draft's clear condemnation of ISIL/Da'esh and its emphasis on sovereignty and humanitarian access. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP4 on unhindered humanitarian access and OP5 on children associated with foreign terrorist fighters, reflecting best-interests-of-the-child and victim-centred treatment. We would also welcome a small addition to OP9 on consultation with humanitarian and human rights actors and Syrian civil society.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft’s condemnation of ISIL/Da’esh and its reaffirmation of Syrian sovereignty and territorial integrity. We ask the penholder to strengthen the language that terrorism must not be associated with any religion or culture, and to make the return and repatriation provisions fully consistent with international refugee law and the principle of non-refoulement. We would also welcome a reference to transparent, fair and evidence-based implementation of sanctions with effective humanitarian exemptions. With these adjustments, Pakistan can support the text.
messages.Panama: Panama supports the draft and thanks the United States for a balanced text. We would like OP5 to state explicitly that returns and repatriations must comply with international law, including non-refoulement and the best interests of the child, and OP9 to include reporting on compliance with international humanitarian and human rights law by all parties. With these adjustments, Panama can join consensus.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the draft’s strong condemnation of ISIL/Da’esh and its focus on foreign terrorist fighters, humanitarian access and accountability. We would like the text to reflect more explicitly the growing terrorist-financing risk from virtual assets and emerging technologies, and to anchor child-associated FTF provisions in the best interests of the child and international law. We can support the remainder of the text and are ready to work with the penholder and other members.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation can support the draft in principle, but the text must be balanced. We request explicit language on non-interference and coordination with the Syrian authorities on humanitarian access, removal of the separate SGBV formulation, and a clear call to lift unilateral coercive measures that undermine humanitarian work and returns. We also ask that the OP9 reporting request be coordinated with the Syrian authorities and not focus on accountability.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone welcomes the draft and supports its strong condemnation of ISIL/Da’esh and reaffirmation of Syrian sovereignty and humanitarian access. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP5 with explicit safeguards for non-refoulement and the best interests of children, and OP3 with a clear reference to FATF standards, which Sierra Leone has consistently highlighted. We also seek survivor-centred language on conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence and modest reporting requirements to ensure the Council receives a gender- and protection-sensitive picture.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the draft's condemnation of ISIL/Da'esh and its focus on humanitarian access and accountability. We ask the penholder to strengthen operative language on IHL and human rights compliance, humanitarian principles, and non-refoulement, especially for children associated with foreign terrorist fighters. These additions are essential for Slovenia's support.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports the draft’s strong condemnation of ISIL/Da’esh and its reaffirmation of sovereignty and humanitarian access. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP3 with capacity-building for frontline and developing States, OP4 with explicit cross-line and cross-border humanitarian access and protection of humanitarian personnel, and OP9 with reporting on regional and cross-border dimensions, including links to ISIL affiliates in Africa. These changes reflect Somalia’s counter-terrorism experience and would enable our delegation to support the text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the United States draft as a strong basis and welcomes this initiative. We would like to see the text strengthen access to Al-Hol and Roj camps, the best interests of children associated with foreign terrorist fighters, and support for the International, Impartial and Independent Mechanism for Syria. We also favour more frequent reporting that explicitly covers implementation of the humanitarian exception in paragraph 10.

replies.China: partially accepted: ETIM named as a Security Council-designated group rather than as an ISIL affiliate; FTF responsibility language accepted; UCM request addressed only through general review/exemption language without explicit lifting or 'unilateral coercive measures' terminology.
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: non-interference accepted and Syrian authority language partially reflected, but SGBV language retained and broadened rather than replaced; UCM request not fully met; reporting keeps accountability while adding Syrian authority consultation.

steps.summary: The revised text incorporates the vast majority of non-P5 and allied requests, including strengthened humanitarian access, child safeguards, non-refoulement language as applicable, accountability, and reporting. China's ETIM and FTF concerns are substantially accommodated, while Russia's core concerns are only partially met, making a Russian abstention the most likely dissent; the draft is expected to command at least 14 votes with no veto.

messages.Algeria: Algeria thanks the penholder for incorporating our previous requests on designated groups, Member State-driven listing and delisting, a non-politicized Monitoring Team, and the principle of non-refoulement. On that basis, Algeria supports the current text and encourages its adoption by consensus. We stress the importance of full respect for Syrian sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-interference, and of effective humanitarian exemptions.
messages.China: China appreciates the penholder’s incorporation of ETIM and the foreign terrorist fighter responsibility language. However, the general language on exemptions and review does not address our core concern over unilateral coercive measures. We request that OP14 explicitly call for the lifting of unilateral coercive measures against Syria that impede humanitarian access and counter-terrorism cooperation. With this adjustment, China is prepared to support the text.
messages.Denmark: Denmark welcomes revision 1 and thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier priorities on international law, children associated with foreign terrorist fighters, and women’s participation. We support the text and have one technical correction: OP11 refers to 'paragraph 12 above', but OP12 appears below. Please correct this cross-reference to 'paragraph 12 of this resolution'; with that fix, Denmark is ready to support the draft.
messages.France: France supports the draft as revised and thanks the United States for incorporating our priorities on humanitarian access, children associated with foreign terrorist fighters, accountability for conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, women’s participation, and the al-Hol and Roj camps. We urge all Council members to support the text and call for its full implementation, including humanitarian exemptions under resolution 2664 (2022) and due-process safeguards. France remains fully committed to the fight against ISIL/Da’esh and to a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process.
messages.Greece: Greece thanks the penholder for incorporating our amendments in revision 1, particularly on non-refoulement, protection of Christians and other minorities, and humanitarian exemptions. We support the current text and believe it strikes the right balance between counter-terrorism, Syria’s sovereignty, and humanitarian and human rights obligations. We encourage all members to unite behind it and to ensure its full, transparent implementation.
messages.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on humanitarian access, children associated with foreign terrorist fighters, and inclusive reporting. We support the current text and will vote in favour; we encourage all Council members to join consensus.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier proposals on dialogue among civilizations, sustainable and non-refoulement-consistent returns, and transparent, evidence-based sanctions with humanitarian and due-process safeguards. We support the current text and call for its full and balanced implementation in strict respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria and all States and for international law. We encourage the Council to remain united against ISIL/Da’esh and all Security Council-designated terrorist groups, including ETIM.
messages.Panama: Panama welcomes the incorporation of its amendments to OP5 and OP9, which strengthen safeguards for children associated with foreign terrorist fighters, affirm non-refoulement, and ensure reporting on compliance with international humanitarian and human rights law. The current text balances counter-terrorism measures with humanitarian access, due-process safeguards and the protection of civilians. Panama supports the draft as it stands and urges the Council to speak with unity and adopt it.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea supports the revised text. We thank the penholder for incorporating our proposals on virtual assets and emerging technologies, capacity-building, child protection, and cooperation with United Nations accountability mechanisms. We urge all Council members to unite behind this balanced text and to ensure full implementation of sanctions, humanitarian access, and accountability.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the draft's counter-terrorism focus and welcomes the acceptance of non-interference, but the text still contains unacceptable references to the IIIM and fails to address unilateral coercive measures. We request the deletion of the IIIM reference, consent-based humanitarian access language, explicit language on lifting unilateral sanctions, and replacement of SGBV terminology with all forms of violence against women and children. These changes are necessary for our support.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the current text as revised. We welcome the incorporation of our priorities, including FATF standards, protection and repatriation of children associated with foreign terrorist fighters, survivor-centred accountability, and reporting on gender, minorities and humanitarian access. We encourage the Council to speak with one voice and adopt the text.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the revised draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating our previous proposals on international law, humanitarian access and non-refoulement, including the protection of children. We believe the text is balanced and operational, and we encourage all Council members to unite behind it and vote in favour.
messages.Somalia: Somalia thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on capacity-building, humanitarian access, and the regional and cross-border dimensions of the threat, including links to ISIL/Da’esh affiliates in Africa. We support the current text and call for its adoption, with emphasis on full implementation, protection of civilians, and technical support to developing States in the region. We encourage continued attention to the African dimension through the reporting requested in OP11.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating our earlier requests on Al-Hol and Roj, children, accountability and reporting. We request one technical correction in OP11: the reference to the humanitarian exception should be to paragraph 12 below, not above. With that correction, we are ready to support the text.

replies.China: partially accepted: added language acknowledging concerns about unilateral coercive measures, but no call for immediate lifting
replies.Russian Federation: partially accepted: deleted explicit IIIM reference, adjusted OP4 and OP11, but retained CRSV language and did not call for lifting unilateral coercive measures

steps.summary: The penholder accepted technical corrections and made targeted compromises on accountability and humanitarian mechanisms while preserving core US priorities on counter-ISIL cooperation, SGBV accountability, and humanitarian exemptions. China and Russia are expected to abstain, yielding adoption with 13 votes in favour and no veto.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria is a firm supporter of international counter-terrorism efforts and the draft reaffirms Syrian sovereignty, non-interference and humanitarian safeguards consistent with Algeria’s positions; no pre-vote explanation is needed.
reasons.China: China supports the resolution's counter-terrorism focus and explicit ETIM reference, and while its OP14 request was only partially accepted, that is not a red line sufficient to abstain given China's consistent support for counter-terrorism resolutions and the draft's reaffirmation of Syrian sovereignty.
reasons.Denmark: Denmark supported the resolution with a minor technical correction, which the penholder accepted, and the text aligns with Denmark’s priorities on counter-terrorism, humanitarian access, accountability and protection of civilians.
reasons.France: France supports the draft’s focus on combating ISIL/Da’esh, humanitarian access, accountability and sanctions implementation, and it raises no blocking concerns. Since the text aligns with France’s priorities and no changes were requested, France votes in favour and does not need to explain its vote before the vote.
reasons.Greece: Greece consistently supports Council counter-terrorism resolutions and had already indicated support without requesting changes; the draft aligns with its priorities on international law, humanitarian access, and protection of minorities.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana supported the previous consensus counter-terrorism resolutions on this agenda item and raised no changes in the last negotiation round; the draft aligns with its stated priorities on sovereignty, humanitarian access and international law. A favourable vote is therefore consistent with its Council record.
reasons.Pakistan: Pakistan has consistently supported UN Security Council counter-terrorism resolutions and the draft aligns with its opposition to terrorism while reflecting concerns about sovereignty, humanitarian access, and sanctions safeguards. No provisions conflict with Pakistan’s core positions, so it votes in favour.
reasons.Panama: Panama supports counter-terrorism resolutions, voted in favour of similar measures, and recorded support without requesting changes. The draft aligns with Panama’s emphasis on international law, humanitarian access, accountability, and Council unity.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently voted in favour of Council counter-terrorism resolutions and supported the United States penholder without requesting changes. The draft reflects ROK priorities on countering terrorism and terrorist financing, humanitarian access and accountability.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia’s core red line—explicit reference to the IIIM—was removed, and the compromise text preserves Syrian sovereignty and consent-based language. Despite remaining concerns over CRSV language and unilateral coercive measures, Russia is likely to vote in favour to maintain counter-terrorism cooperation and avoid blocking a resolution that reflects key Russian priorities.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supported the last negotiation round, requested no changes, and consistently backs robust, rights-compliant counter-terrorism and 1267 sanctions measures. The draft includes priorities important to Sierra Leone, including FATF standards, SGBV accountability, humanitarian exemptions, child protection and Africa-related terrorist financing links.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia supported the previous consensus counter-terrorism resolution and has no outstanding requests; the draft aligns with its priorities on humanitarian access, accountability, children, gender, and international-law safeguards. A yes vote is consistent with its established Council record and coalition positions.
reasons.Somalia: Somalia has consistently prioritized counter-terrorism cooperation, especially against ISIL/Da’esh-linked and cross-border threats affecting Africa, and it supported the draft without requests. A statement reinforces its support for sovereignty, humanitarian access, and international law.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK supported the draft in negotiations, its minor cross-reference request was accepted, and the text aligns with UK priorities on counter-terrorism, humanitarian access, accountability and human rights. As a P5 with a consistent record of supporting this agenda item, the UK votes in favour.
reasons.United States of America: The draft was submitted by the United States and aligns with U.S. counterterrorism priorities in Syria. As penholder and a permanent member, the United States would vote in favour and explain its support before the vote.

before.China: China will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We welcome the reaffirmation of Syria’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity, and the explicit reference to the East Turkestan Islamic Movement as a terrorist entity designated by the Security Council. China supports the international community’s counter-terrorism efforts and believes that counter-terrorism in Syria must be comprehensive, respect national sovereignty and avoid politicization. At the same time, China has consistently opposed unilateral coercive measures, which violate international law, exacerbate the suffering of the Syrian people and impede humanitarian access and counter-terrorism cooperation. We regret that the draft only acknowledges concerns about unilateral coercive measures and does not call for their immediate lifting, as China proposed. We hope the Council will address this issue seriously in its future work. Humanitarian access should be delivered in accordance with international humanitarian law, the humanitarian principles and respect for Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. China will vote in favour.
before.Denmark: Denmark votes in favour of this resolution. We thank the United States for its leadership and for accepting our correction to the cross-reference in operative paragraph 11. The text sends a clear message that ISIL/Da’esh and all terrorist groups in Syria must be denied safe haven, financing, recruitment and the ability to plan attacks, and that the territory of Syria must not be used for terrorist acts. Denmark attaches particular importance to safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians, accountability for terrorism and conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, and the best interests of children associated with foreign terrorist fighters, including those in Al-Hol and Roj. We also underline that counter-terrorism measures must be implemented in full compliance with international law and that humanitarian exemptions must be applied in practice.
before.Greece: Greece votes in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly condemn all terrorist acts by ISIL/Da’esh and its affiliates, and we support strengthened international cooperation against terrorism, terrorist financing and foreign terrorist fighters. We welcome the resolution’s reaffirmation of Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, its demands for safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and its focus on accountability, protection of civilians, and the rights of women, children and persons belonging to minorities, including Christian communities. Greece stresses that all counter-terrorism measures must be implemented in full compliance with international law, including human rights, refugee and humanitarian law, and that humanitarian exemptions and due-process safeguards must be applied effectively.
before.Guyana: Guyana thanks the penholder for its constructive approach and will vote in favour of this draft. We support strengthened Council action against ISIL/Da’esh and all designated terrorist groups in Syria, while stressing that counter-terrorism measures must be implemented in full compliance with international law, including human rights, refugee and humanitarian law. Guyana underscores the importance of preserving Syria’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity, ensuring safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, protecting children and vulnerable persons, and applying the humanitarian exemptions under resolution 2664 (2022). We also stress the need for accountability, gender-sensitive approaches, and transparent, fair and evidence-based sanctions implementation.
before.Pakistan: Pakistan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. As a country that has suffered greatly from terrorism, Pakistan firmly supports international efforts against ISIL/Da’esh and all terrorist groups designated by the Security Council. At the same time, we stress that counter-terrorism measures must be implemented in full respect for the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Syria and all States, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations and international law. We also underline the need for safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, transparent and evidence-based sanctions with due-process and humanitarian safeguards, and a comprehensive approach that addresses the conditions conducive to terrorism and avoids associating terrorism with any religion, nationality or civilization. Pakistan calls for strengthened international and regional cooperation, including capacity-building for developing countries, to prevent and suppress terrorist acts.
before.Panama: Mr. President, Panama voted in favour of this draft because we unequivocally condemn terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including ISIL/Da’esh and all Security Council-designated terrorist groups in Syria. We believe the Council must act with unity while fully respecting the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of Syria and all States, and while ensuring that counter-terrorism measures do not impede humanitarian assistance. Panama also supports the text’s emphasis on accountability, the protection of civilians, the rights and best interests of children, and transparent, fair and evidence-based sanctions implementation with effective humanitarian exemptions and due-process safeguards. For these reasons, Panama will vote in favour.
before.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly condemn all terrorist acts by ISIL/Da’esh, its affiliates, ETIM and other Security Council-designated terrorist groups in Syria. We support strengthened international cooperation against terrorist financing, foreign terrorist fighters and cross-border threats, while reaffirming Syria’s sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity. We also underscore the importance of safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability for terrorist crimes, and full implementation of the 1267 sanctions regime with due-process safeguards and humanitarian exemptions. The Republic of Korea remains committed to a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation consistently supports international efforts to combat ISIL/Da’esh and all terrorist groups in Syria. We welcome that the draft reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of the Syrian Arab Republic and the principle of non-interference in its internal affairs. We also note that the text recognizes the need to coordinate humanitarian access with the Syrian authorities and contains a reference to the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures. However, we emphasize that any accountability measures must be implemented in accordance with national law and with the consent of the Syrian authorities and must not be used to create parallel mechanisms that undermine Syrian sovereignty. We call for the lifting of unilateral sanctions that worsen the humanitarian situation. On this basis, the Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone votes in favour of this draft resolution. We do so because it condemns terrorism in all its forms, reaffirms the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria and all States, and strengthens the international legal and sanctions framework against ISIL/Da’esh, its affiliates and other Council-designated terrorist groups. Sierra Leone welcomes the draft’s emphasis on countering terrorist financing, implementing FATF standards, addressing virtual assets and emerging technologies, and building the capacity of developing countries in the region. We also value its attention to humanitarian access, the protection of civilians, accountability for conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, the rights and best interests of children, and the need for sanctions to be implemented transparently and with effective humanitarian exemptions and due-process safeguards. We encourage all Member States to cooperate fully with the 1267 Committee and the Monitoring Team, including on the growing links between ISIL/Da’esh affiliates in Syria and terrorist networks in Africa, and to ensure that counter-terrorism measures do not impede principled humanitarian action.
before.Slovenia: Slovenia votes in favour of this draft resolution. We strongly condemn all terrorist acts by ISIL/Da’esh, its affiliates and other Security Council-designated groups in Syria, and we support strengthening international cooperation to prevent their resurgence. Slovenia welcomes the draft’s emphasis on the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Syria, safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, accountability for terrorist crimes and conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, and the prioritisation of the best interests of children associated with foreign terrorist fighters. We also stress that all counter-terrorism and sanctions measures must be implemented in full compliance with international law, including human rights law, refugee law and international humanitarian law, with transparent, fair and effective humanitarian exemptions and due-process safeguards.
before.Somalia: Mr. President, Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. Terrorism, including ISIL/Da’esh and its affiliates, constitutes a serious threat to international peace and security, including through cross-border movement, terrorist financing and links to terrorist networks in Africa. We support strengthened international cooperation against terrorism while reaffirming the sovereignty, territorial integrity and independence of Syria and all States, and we underline the need for safe, unhindered humanitarian access to civilians, protection of children and vulnerable persons, accountability for terrorist crimes, and full compliance with international law, including international humanitarian law and human rights law.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. We welcome the correction of the cross-reference in OP11 and the text’s clear condemnation of ISIL/Da’esh, ETIM and all Council-designated terrorist groups in Syria. The United Kingdom remains committed to Syria’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and national unity, and to ensuring that counter-terrorism measures do not impede principled humanitarian action. We underline the need for safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians including minorities and children, accountability for terrorist crimes and conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, and the repatriation, rehabilitation and reintegration of foreign terrorist fighters and associated persons, with the best interests of the child paramount. We also stress that sanctions implementation must remain transparent, fair, evidence-based and consistent with robust humanitarian exemptions and due-process safeguards.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. The continued threat posed by ISIL/Da’esh in Syria demands a unified and effective Council response, and this text strengthens our collective ability to prevent the resurgence of terrorism, deny safe haven, cut off financing, and ensure accountability. It also underscores the imperative of safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and the repatriation and reintegration of foreign terrorist fighters and associated persons, especially children. We thank Council members for their constructive engagement and urge full implementation of the measures set out in this resolution.

after.Algeria:
Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. We condemn terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including ISIL/Da’esh, its affiliates and all terrorist groups designated by the Security Council in Syria. We supported this text because it reaffirms the sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity of Syria and all States, and because it strengthens international cooperation against terrorist financing, foreign terrorist fighters and the resurgence of terrorist networks.

At the same time, Algeria stresses that all counter-terrorism measures must be implemented in full respect for the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and the principle of non-interference in the internal affairs of States. Counter-terrorism must not be politicized or selective, and terrorism must never be associated with any religion, nationality, civilization or ethnic group. Sustainable progress requires advancing a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015), national reconciliation and efforts to address the conditions conducive to terrorism.

We also underscore that sanctions must remain transparent, fair and evidence-based, with due-process and humanitarian safeguards. Listing and delisting processes should preserve their Member State-driven character, and the work of sanctions monitoring mechanisms must not be politicized. Humanitarian access must be safe, rapid, sustained and unhindered for all civilians in need, in accordance with humanitarian principles, and must not be impeded by unilateral coercive measures or other obstacles.

Algeria remains committed to constructive engagement and to the unity of the Security Council in confronting the common threat of terrorism.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France voted in favour of this resolution. We thank the United States for its work as penholder.

The adoption of this text sends a clear message: the continued presence and potential resurgence of Da’esh and its affiliates in Syria must be prevented. All terrorist groups designated by the Security Council, including ETIM, must be denied safe haven, financing, recruitment, planning and the ability to carry out attacks. France remains fully engaged in the fight against Da’esh and will continue to act with its partners against terrorism.

At the same time, counter-terrorism measures must be implemented in full compliance with international law, including international human rights law, international humanitarian law and international refugee law. We reaffirm the need to respect Syria’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity, and to support a genuine Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).

France stresses the imperative of safe, rapid, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syria, including to Al-Hol and Roj camps and detention facilities. The protection of civilians, in particular women, children, persons belonging to minorities and other vulnerable persons, must remain central. Children associated with foreign terrorist fighters must be treated first and foremost as children, and repatriation, rehabilitation and reintegration should be pursued in line with international law and the best interests of the child.

Accountability for terrorist crimes is essential, including for conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence and the crimes committed against Yazidis and other communities. Sanctions must continue to be implemented fully and fairly, with due-process guarantees and humanitarian safeguards, including those under resolution 2664 (2022). France will remain actively engaged in ensuring the full implementation of this resolution.
after.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation voted in favour of the adopted resolution. We support effective counter-terrorism measures against ISIL/Da’esh, its affiliates, the East Turkestan Islamic Movement and all terrorist groups designated by the Security Council in Syria. We welcome the reaffirmation of Syria’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and national unity and the principle of non-interference in its internal affairs. We also note the text’s recognition of the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures. At the same time, we stress that this resolution must be implemented in strict compliance with the Charter of the United Nations and with full respect for Syrian sovereignty. Humanitarian access should be ensured in coordination with the Syrian authorities. Accountability for terrorist crimes must be pursued in accordance with national law and with the consent of the Syrian authorities, and must not be used to create parallel mechanisms that undermine sovereignty. We reiterate our call for the lifting of unilateral sanctions, which aggravate the humanitarian situation and complicate counter-terrorism efforts. We will carefully monitor the implementation of this resolution and oppose any attempt to use it for political pressure or interference in Syria’s internal affairs.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United States welcomes the Security Council’s unanimous adoption of this resolution. We thank Council members for their constructive engagement and for working with the penholder to strengthen the text, including the correction to the cross-reference in operative paragraph 11.

Today’s vote sends a clear and unified message that ISIL/Da’esh, its affiliates, ETIM, and all other Security Council-designated terrorist groups in Syria must be denied safe haven, financing, recruitment, and the ability to plan and carry out attacks. The Council has reaffirmed that the territory of Syria and of all States must not be used for terrorist acts, and that counter-terrorism cooperation must be strengthened, including through border security, countering terrorist financing, and addressing virtual assets and emerging technologies.

The United States also underscores that this resolution is clear on the protection of civilians and the imperative of safe, rapid, sustained, and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syria, including in Al-Hol and Roj camps and detention facilities. We welcome the text’s emphasis on accountability for terrorist crimes, including conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, and on the best interests of children associated with foreign terrorist fighters. We reaffirm that counter-terrorism measures must be implemented in full compliance with international law, including international human rights law, refugee law, and international humanitarian law, and consistent with the humanitarian exemptions under resolution 2664 (2022).

The United States remains committed to Syria’s sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity, and national unity, and to a Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015). Adoption is only the first step; full implementation is now essential. The United States will continue to work with all Council members and partners to ensure that this resolution contributes to real progress in denying terrorists the ability to threaten international peace and security.
